subject: science

entries: Exothermic: products lie below reactants: the profile falls from the reactants level to a lower products level, so ΔH is negative and heat leaves the system.
slots.label: Exothermic
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Endothermic: products lie above reactants: the profile climbs to a higher products level, so ΔH is positive and heat is absorbed from the surroundings.
slots.label: Endothermic
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Rate curves: steeper means faster: the gradient of the concentration-time curve is the rate, and higher temperature or a catalyst makes the curve steeper.
slots.label: Rate curves
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Maxwell–Boltzmann: more molecules past Ea at higher T: the distribution flattens and shifts right, so a bigger fraction of molecules can react on collision.
slots.label: Maxwell–Boltzmann
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Le Chatelier: the system opposes the change: adding a reactant or raising the pressure shifts the Haber equilibrium to oppose the disturbance, while Kc changes only with temperature.
slots.label: Le Chatelier
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: a catalyst shifts equilibrium: both rates grow by the same factor, the composition bars never move, and the equilibrium position and Kc stay unchanged.
slots.label: A common mistake
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The heat change at constant pressure, ΔH: products minus reactants on a reaction profile - negative for exothermic, positive for endothermic.
slots.label: Enthalpy change
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The minimum energy Ea a collision needs for reaction to occur: on a reaction profile it is the climb from the reactants level to the transition state.
slots.label: Activation energy
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: How fast reactant concentration falls, rate = -Δ[R] / Δt: read from the gradient of a concentration-time curve, steeper meaning faster.
slots.label: Rate of reaction
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A substance that speeds up a reaction by providing a lower-activation-energy route, and is chemically unchanged at the end: it speeds forward and reverse reactions equally.
slots.label: Catalyst
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The state of a reversible reaction in a closed system where the forward and reverse rates are equal and concentrations stay constant.
slots.label: Dynamic equilibrium
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The spread of molecular kinetic energies at a temperature: most molecules sit near the average, and only the tail past Ea can react on collision.
slots.label: Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
